subject: Week 24: allergens are a cadence — peanut and egg 2-3x weekly
bodyText:
This week
By the end of days 166-172, most starter eaters have tried 5-10 foods, and self-feeding intent shows up — deliberate hand-to-mouth, objects transferring hand to hand. Sitting is steadying with support and solid for some, though the CDC sits-without-support checkpoint remains 9 months, so support is still the expected default. Babble strings with varied consonants and delighted mirror games round out the week.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Stool changes color and consistency on solids — beets and blueberries pass through visibly. Normal.
- [monitor] Frequent gagging at meals — gagging is loud and protective; choking is silent. Also monitor constipation lasting past three days.
- [call within 24h] Hives beyond the mouth area or repeated vomiting inside two hours of a new food — note the food and call.
- [call now] Choking with no air movement — no cough, no cry: back blows and chest thrusts (never abdominal thrusts at this age) and 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Build the allergen calendar: once first foods are tolerated, introduce peanut (1 tsp smooth peanut butter thinned in warm water, or softened peanut puffs) and well-cooked egg, then hold peanut, egg, dairy, wheat, and soy each at 2-3x weekly. One new allergen at a time, in the morning, at home, with a 2-hour observation window. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Book an infant CPR and choking class before finger foods scale up — the infant protocol is back blows plus chest thrusts, and the Red Cross runs classes weekly across the city.
- Lock the weekly SFPL Baby Rhyme & Play Time slot onto the standing calendar if it is not there already — free, ticketed same-day at popular branches, and the Cantonese and Spanish sessions double as live second-language exposure. SFPL storytimes: https://sfpl.org/kids/kids/events/storytime-sfpl
- Practice standing: hold his hands and let him bear weight in short bouts — leg strength now feeds pulling-to-stand and cruising later. AAP: Movement 4-7 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-4-to-7-Months.aspx
- Keep one true family meal a day — adult conversation around him beats solo high-chair time, and conversational turns are the language input that shows up on brain imaging (Romeo et al. 2018). Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26–Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit window is open. Vaccines: RV #3 (if RV5), DTaP #3, Hib #3 (if PRP-T), PCV #3, seasonal influenza #1; iron/hemoglobin screen. Bring the sleep log and feeding plan.
- Day 180 (Nov 7, 2026): three 6-month windows open at once — swim converts to paid, ISR instructor lists open, and the Suzuki instrument decision comes due.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Supports whole weight on legs when held standing
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Builds leg strength for eventual pulling-to-stand. Does not need to bear weight independently.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/supports-weight-on-legs/complete

- Moves things from one hand to the other
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Bilateral coordination across the midline. Often accompanied by mouthing the transferred object.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/transfers-objects-hand-to-hand/complete

- Closes lips to show she doesn't want more food
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Pre-verbal refusal. Important to respect — supports developing satiety cues.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/closes-lips-not-more/complete

- Enjoys back-and-forth social play
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Active turn-taking in physical or vocal games. Distinct from earlier passive enjoyment of stimulation.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/enjoys-social-play/complete

- Sits without support
  AAP window: day 150-270
  What to look for: Hands free for play. WHO motor study cites 3.8-9.2 mo as the typical range.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-without-support/complete
